title: A Physics-Informed Clustering and Class-Balanced Machine Learning Framework for Industrial Pump Health Monitoring
content: This research presents a multi-stage methodology for analyzing and predicting industrial pump fleet health using sensor data. Following exploratory data analysis, a K-means++ clustering algorithm segmented the data into distinct operational states. Statistical validation confirmed significant variance in variable means across clusters. A physics-informed labeling strategy subsequently mapped these clusters to four domain-specific health states: Normal, Healthy, Impending Failure, and End of Life. The resulting dataset was utilized to evaluate multiple classification architectures. The Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) framework emerged as the optimal model. Optimized via Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, this architecture successfully countered severe class prevalence asymmetry, yielding high sensitivity for the critical Impending Failure minority state label while effectively resolving overlapping physical transition boundaries. The framework achieved robust predictive performance across training and unseen validation datasets. To ensure transparency and foster operator trust, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) were integrated to provide instance-level feature contributions, delineating the specific sensor thresholds triggering health-state predictions. Ultimately, this work demonstrates the efficacy of integrating unsupervised and supervised learning frameworks with domain expertise to deliver robust, explainable predictive maintenance solutions.
